To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SOAP is the first system that can schedule online data repartitioning in a distributed OLAP system without disrupting normal transactions.

(1) we have proposed a system framework SOAP for scheduling online database (re)partitioning, (2) we have developed a cost model to guide the scheduling of repartition operations, (3) we have developed an online feedback model to dynamically adjust the repartition scheduling strategy, and (4) we have built a prototype and evaluated its performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a problem that has been overlooked in the database community, but is critical to the practical deployment of automatic data partitioning in distributed database systems.
the problem of online data partitioning in distributed database systems.
a problem about how to schedule the repartition operation in the context of a distributed OLTP workload.

the proposed framework SOAP has been successfully implemented and evaluated.
the SOAP system is a very promising and practical system for online data partitioning in distributed database systems.
the SOAP approach is a significant contribution to the field of distributed database partitioning and scheduling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SOAP can effectively reduce the repartition time by more than 50% and improve the overall system throughput by up to 20%.
SOAP provides a holistic approach to scheduling online database repartonition in distributed database systems.
, we propose a novel approach to scheduling online data repartitioning in OLTP systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the online data partitioning problem in distributed database system is not a simple problem and should be addressed with holistic optimization.
online database partitioning can be efficiently and effectively performed on top of a modern database engine without interrupting the processing of normal OLTP transactions.
